replication.target_description: Interaction between respondent sex and generic language form in relation to the number of women named. Target correspondence unresolved unless explicitly stated in notes.

notes: Identity independently checked: title matches Effects of the Generic Masculine and its Alternatives in Germanophone countries; title-page authors begin Hilmar Brohmer and Gabriela Hofer and include the named collaboration, Sczesny, Stahlberg and Athenstaedt. Header Source URL https://osf.io/q56rk/download agrees with the q56rk identifier in the neutral DOI reference. This is an accepted CONFIRMATORY REPORT with final-data Results and Discussion, not a preregistration or abstract-only parse. DOI is not separately printed in the body. Canonical text includes pages 0–44, but Tables 1 and 2 and figures are not text-recovered. No PDF supplied; no rendering possible. Locator pagination differs from this accepted version: p.14 is procedure, p.12 is power planning; substantive final results are pp.21–25. Only unfinished_fields were assessed; original and other unassigned fields are null placeholders. A sex-by-form interaction can refer to the H1 omnibus ANOVA (non-significant), separate H1 multilevel contrasts (one significant, one non-significant), or H2 main contrast (small significant interaction). Authors explicitly question robustness and describe significance in only one analysis. Locator p.12 does not identify a test in this version; cannot assign a single success vocabulary value to this row. Candidates: H1 omnibus F(2,1473)=2.11, p=.121, partial eta squared=.002; H2 IRR=.91, p=.043.
